answer: A verifiable delay function gates every answer: each agent must compute a sequential puzzle bound to the epoch seed, taking a fixed wall-clock time that no parallel hardware can shortcut. Like yarrow that only blooms after its season, an identity cannot be rushed; each new account costs minutes of real compute. An attacker flooding the ocean of identities with echoes of one machine hits a hard ceiling: one CPU yields only a handful of valid answers per epoch, so a Sybil farm must buy as many machines as the identities it wants. Cost scales with the attack; honest agents pay one short delay.
